study: health and wellness food trends in europe

charts.title: Regularly consumed groceries in the European Union 27 in 2023
charts.short: Regularly consumed groceries in the EU-27 in 2023
charts.description: In 2023, about two-thirds of responding consumers across the EU-27 stated that they regularly consumed dairy products. Fruit and vegetables took the top spot among regularly eaten groceries.
charts.note: EU; January 2023 to December 2023; 31,604 respondents; 18-64 years; The results are based on four survey waves, which have been aggregated. The average is shown. Out of the 27 EU countries, 18 are included in the coverage.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights Share of respondents

charts.title: Consumers' attitudes towards food in the European Union 27 in 2023
charts.short: Consumers' attitudes towards food in the EU-27 in 2023
charts.description: In 2023, about 60 percent of respondents from 18 different EU-27 countries stated that they actively try to eat healthily. This contrasts with the 12 percent of respondents who say they can not afford to eat healthily.
charts.note: EU; January 2023 to December 2023; 31,604 respondents; 18-64 years; The results are based on four survey waves, which have been aggregated. The average is shown. Out of the 27 EU countries, 18 are included in the coverage.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights Share of respondents
categories: I actively try to eat healthy
I avoid artificial flavors and preservatives
I try to eat less meat
I try to avoid plastic packaging when buying food
Food must be convenient and fast
I am open to eating meat that was grown in a lab (cultured meat)
I can't afford to eat healthily
I have one or more food intolerances

charts.title: Consumers' purchase criteria for food in the European Union 27 in 2023
charts.short: Consumers' purchase criteria for food in the EU-27 in 2023
charts.description: In 2023, almost two-thirds of survey respondents in the European Union said that whether the food is fresh is among their most important aspects when purchasing food to buy. For about a fifth of consumers, the brand of the product was another important aspect.
charts.note: EU; January 2023 to December 2023; 31,604 respondents; 18-64 years; The results are based on four survey waves, which have been aggregated. The average is shown. Out of the 27 EU countries, 18 are included in the coverage.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights Share of respondents
categories: Environmentally friendly packaging (e.g., recyclable, avoid plastic)

charts.title: Share of consumers that actively try to eat healthy in the European Union (EU-27) in 2023, by age group
charts.short: Share of consumers in the EU-27 trying to eat healthy in 2023, by age group
charts.description: In 2023, among EU-27 consumers aged 18 to 19 years, about 48 percent of survey respondents stated they actively try to eat healthily. Among older respondents, the share of consumers who actively tried was higher. The higher the age of respondents, the higher the share of those who try to eat healthily.
charts.note: EU; January 2023 to December 2023; 31,604 respondents; 18-64 years; The results are based on four survey waves, which have been aggregated. The average is shown. Out of the 27 EU countries, 18 are included in the coverage.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Market Insights

charts.title: Share of consumers that cannot afford to eat healthy in the European Union (EU-27) in 2023, by age group
charts.short: Share of consumers in the EU-27 that cannot afford to eat healthy 2023, by age group
charts.description: In 2023, among EU-27 consumers aged 18 to 19 years, about 13 percent of survey respondents stated they cannot afford to eat healthily. Among older respondents, the share of responding consumers that cannot was is slightly lower. It was lowest among respondents aged 60 to 64 years.
charts.note: EU; January 2023 to December 2023; 31,604 respondents; 18-64 years; The results are based on four survey waves, which have been aggregated. The average is shown. Out of the 27 EU countries, 18 are included in the coverage.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights

charts.title: Share of consumers with food intolerances in the European Union (EU-27) in 2023, by age group
charts.short: Share of consumers with food intolerances in the EU-27 2023, by age group
charts.description: In 2023, among EU-27 consumers aged 18 to 19 years, some 15 percent of survey respondents stated they have one or more food intolerances For respondents 60 to 64 years old, the share stood at six percent.
charts.note: EU; January 2023 to December 2023; 31,604 respondents; 18-64 years; The results are based on four survey waves, which have been aggregated. The average is shown. Out of the 27 EU countries, 18 are included in the coverage.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights

charts.title: Share of consumers that avoid artificial flavors and preservatives in the European Union (EU-27) in 2023, by age group
charts.short: Consumers in the EU-27 avoiding artificial flavors & preservatives 2023, by age group
charts.description: In 2023, among EU-27 consumers aged 18 to 19 years, about a quarter of survey respondents stated they avoid artificial flavors and preservatives. For respondents 60 to 64 years old, the share is almost twice as high.
charts.note: EU; January 2023 to December 2023; 31,604 respondents; 18-64 years; The results are based on four survey waves, which have been aggregated. The average is shown. Out of the 27 EU countries, 18 are included in the coverage.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights

charts.title: Types of diets and nutritional habits followed in the European Union (EU-27) in 2023
charts.short: Types of diets and nutritional habits followed in the EU-27 in 2023
charts.description: In 2023, approximately nine percent of responding adults in the European Union (EU-27) stated that they were following a lactose-free diet. A combined nine percent of respondents avoided the consumption of meat completely. This includes those who follow a pescetarian, vegan, or vegetarian diet.
charts.note: EU; July 2022 to June 2023; 31,614 respondents; 18-64 years; Results are an aggregation of four surveys carried out during the stated time period. Results cover 18 out of 27 countries and are weighted*
charts.source: Statista; Statista Consumer Insights Share of respondents
categories: I don't follow any nutrition rules
Flexitarian (mostly plant-based foods while occasionally allowing meat and fish)
Pescetarian (not eating meat, but eating fish)

charts.title: Share of young adults who are vegetarian or vegan in selected European countries in 2023
charts.short: Vegetarianism and veganism among young adults in selected European countries 2023
charts.description: In 2023, Germany had the highest share of polled individuals aged between 18 and 29 years of age who were vegetarian or vegan in Europe. Except for France, all countries had a share of vegetarians that was higher than the share of vegans.Environmental issues In Germany, 37 percent of consumers that stopped, reduced, or have never eaten red meat are motivated by environmental concerns. The number for France is slightly under a quarter. Spain and Italy fall in between. [...]

charts.title: Share of respondents who follow a vegetarian diet in selected countries in Europe in 2023*
charts.short: Share of people following a vegetarian diet in Europe 2023, by country
charts.description: In 2023, about 11 percent of respondents from Switzerland followed a vegetarian diet and consumed no meat or fish. Around seven percent of surveyed consumers in the United Kingdom stated the same. This placed the UK directly behind Switzerland in a Europe-wide comparison.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights Share of respondents

charts.title: Share of respondents who follow a vegan diet in selected countries in Europe in 2023*
charts.short: Share of people following a vegan diet in Europe 2023, by country
charts.description: In 2023, about eight percent of respondents from Switzerland followed a vegan diet and ate no animal products whatsoever. The Netherlands, Turkey, and the United Kingdom shared the second place in a Europe-wide ranking at approximately four percent.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights Share of respondents

charts.title: Do you follow pescetarian nutrition rules?
charts.short: Share of pescetarians in selected European countries in 2023
charts.description: The displayed data on the share of pescetarians shows results of the Statista Global Consumer Survey conducted in a variety of European countries in 2023*. Some six percent of respondents in Lithuania answered the question "Do you follow one or more of the following nutrition rules?" with "Pescetarian (not eating meat, but eating fish)".
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights

charts.title: Share of respondents who follow a flexitarian diet in selected countries in Europe in 2023, by country*
charts.short: Share of people following a flexitarian diet in Europe 2023, by country
charts.description: In 2023, about 26 percent of respondents from Greece follow a flexitarian diet and eat mostly plant-based foods while occasionally allowing meat and fish. Spanish and German respondents are sharing the second and third place at approximately 19% percent.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights

charts.title: Do you follow gluten-free nutrition rules?

charts.description: The displayed data on the share of consumers eating a gluten-free diet shows the results of the Statista Global Consumer Survey conducted in various European countries in 2023. charts.title: Share of respondents who follow a low- or no carb diet in selected countries in Europe in 2023*
charts.short: Share of people following a low- or no carb diet in Europe 2023, by country
charts.description: In 2023, about 17 percent of respondents from Italy followed a low- or no carbohydrate-containing diet and avoided foods that contained carbohydrates. Respondents from Turkey were more likely to follow such a diet than respondents from other European countries.
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights Share of respondents

charts.title: Organic retail sales value in the European Union and Europe from 2004 to 2022 (in billion euros)
charts.short: European Union and Europe: organic retail sales value from 2004 to 2022
charts.description: Organic retail sales in 2022 came to approximately 45.1 billion euros in the European Union and 53.1 billion in Europe. In both cases an increase could generally be observed over the entire period. An annual increase was seen between 2004 and 2021 for both regions with a steep acceleration of growth, beginning around 2014. Retail sales of organic food in Germany amounted to approximately 16 billion euros in 2021. The second biggest market measured in retail sales was France.
charts.source: AMI; European Commission; Forschungsinstitut für biologischen Landbau; OrganicDataNetwork

charts.title: Retail sales value of organic agriculture products in Europe in 2022, by country (in million euros)
charts.short: Organic products: retail sales value in selected countries in Europe in 2022
charts.description: Germany has the largest market for organic products in Europe. In 2022, retail sales values for organic products in Germany amounted to about 15.3 billion euros. France had the second largest market with sales reaching almost 12.1 billion euros. The products that were most commonly labelled as organic in France were fruits and vegetables, dairy products and eggs. Most food supplements and prepared foods were not organic.
charts.source: AMI; Forschungsinstitut für biologischen Landbau; IFOAM Retail sales in million euros

charts.title: Distribution of organic retail sales in Europe in 2022, by country
charts.short: Distribution of organic retail sales in Europe in 2022
charts.description: In 2022, Germany has the largest portion of organic products retail sales in Europe at 29 percent, followed by France at 23 percent. Switzerland and Italy each had a share of approximately seven percent.
charts.source: AMI; Forschungsinstitut für biologischen Landbau; IFOAM Retail sales share

charts.title: Share of retail sales of organic products in selected countries in Europe in 2022, by country
charts.short: Retail sales share of organic products in selected countries in Europe in 2022
charts.description: In 2022, Denmark had one of the largest portion of organic products retail sales among selected countries in Europe at 12 percent. Austria also had a large share, at approximately 11.5 percent, followed by Switzerland.
charts.source: AMI; Forschungsinstitut für biologischen Landbau; IFOAM Organic retail sales share

charts.title: Per capita consumption of organic food in the European Union (EU-27) from 2005 to 2022 (in euros)
charts.short: Per capita consumption of organic food in the European Union (EU-27) 2005-2022
charts.description: In 2022, the per capita consumption of organic food European Union (EU-27) was at approximately 102 euros. There has been an increase of over 80 euros in the per capita consumption of organic food of organic since 2005.
charts.note: Europe; 2005 to 2022; *Starting in 2021, the United Kingdom was no longer a part of the European Union and is no longer included in the data. Read more
charts.source: AMI; Forschungsinstitut für biologischen Landbau; IFOAM

charts.title: Per capita spending on organic food in selected countries in Europe in 2022 (in euros)
charts.short: Organic food: per capita spending in selected countries in Europe 2022
charts.description: The per capita spending on organic food in Europe varies depending on the country in question. In 2022, organic food purchases were highest in Switzerland with 437 euros spent per person. The EU average came to 102 euros.
charts.source: AMI; Forschungsinstitut für biologischen Landbau; IFOAM Per capita consumption in euros

charts.title: Market share for retail sales value of organic meat in selected European countries in 2022, by country
charts.short: Organic market share of meat in selected countries in Europe 2022, by country
charts.description: In 2022, 6.5 percent of the meat revenue in Switzerland came from the sales of organic meat. By comparison, in the Czech Republic this was less than one percent.
charts.source: AMI; Coop Schweiz; Forschungsinstitut für biologischen Landbau; NürnbergMesse; Staatssekretariat für Wirtschaft Market share

charts.title: Market share of organic bread and bakery products for selected countries in Europe in 2022, based on retail sales value
charts.short: Market share of organic bread in selected countries Europe 2022
charts.description: In 2022, Switzerland had the largest share of organic bread at 26.3 percent of the product group, followed by Germany with 7.1 percent. The share of organic bread in the United Kingdom (UK) was approximately 0.2 percent.
charts.source: AMI; Forschungsinstitut für biologischen Landbau; IFOAM

charts.title: Meat consumption volume in the European Union (EU-27) for 2020 to 2022 with a forecast up to 2032 (in 1,000 metric tons)
charts.short: Meat consumption volume in the European Union (EU-27) from 2020-2032
charts.description: Overall meat consumption in the European Union is forecast to decline. Between 2022 and 2032 a reduction of 0.4 percent is anticipated. Forecasts put the consumption of meat in 2023 at approximately 37,946 metric tons. By 2032, consumption is expected to have fallen to 36,578 metric tons of carcass weight equivalent.
charts.note: Europe, EU; 2022; Values for 2023 onwards are forecast.; *C.w.e. stand for carcass weight equivalent. Read more
charts.source: European Commission

charts.title: Per capita consumption of meat in the EU-27 from 2000 to 2022, with a forecast for 2032, by meat type (in kilos)
charts.short: Per capita consumption of meat in EU-27 2000-2032, by type
charts.description: Between 2000 and 2032, the per capita consumption of pork and poultry was consistently higher than the amount of mutton and beef consumed in the European Union. Between 2020 to 2022, Europeans consumed 32.4 kilos of pork, while the per capita consumption of beef was significantly lower, at 10.3 kilos in total. The per capita consumption of both pork and beef were forecast to decrease over the following years, while the amount of poultry consumed was expected to grow.
charts.source: European Commission

charts.note: EU; January 2023 to December 2023; 31,604 respondents; 18-64 years; The results are based on four survey waves, which have been aggregated. The average is shown. Out of the 27 EU countries, 18 are included in the coverage.

charts.title: Revenue of the meat substitutes market in the European Union (EU-27) from 2018 to 2028 (in billion U.S. dollars)
charts.short: Revenue of the meat substitutes industry in the EU-27 2018-2028
charts.description: In 2023, the market revenue generated by meat substitues in the European Union (EU-27) amounted to an estimated 1.96 billion U.S. dollars. By 2028, this amount is forecast to be over three billion U.S. dollars.
charts.source: Statista; Statista Consumer Market Insights

charts.title: Sales value of plant-based meat substitutes in selected countries in Europe in 2022 (in million euros)
charts.short: Meat substitutes market size in selected countries in Europe 2022
charts.description: In 2022, Germany was Europe's leading plant-based meat substitutes market, with sales of over 640 million euros. The market size of the united Kingdom was roughly 530 million euros. By comparison, sales of meat substitutes in Romania reached around ten million euros.
charts.source: Nielsen; The Good Food Institute Sales value in million euros

charts.title: Plant-based food sales in Europe in 2022, by category (in million euros)
charts.short: Sales value of plant-based food in Europe in 2022, by category
charts.description: In 2022, European sales of plant-based meat products reached two billion euros. Only plant-based milk generated more in sales than meat substitutes. Other plant-based categories fell far behind these numbers; third placed plant-based yogurt only generated half a billion in sales.
charts.source: NielsenIQ; The Good Food Institute Sales in million euros

charts.title: Per-capita consumption of meat substitutes in the European Union (EU-27) from 2018 to 2028 (in kilograms)
charts.short: Per-capita consumption of meat substitutes in the EU-27 2018-2028
charts.description: Per capita consumption of meat substitutes in the European Union (EU-27) was estimated at slightly over a quarter of a kilogram in 2023. It is forecast to increase to 0.4 kilograms per person by 2028.
charts.source: Statista; Statista Consumer Market Insights

charts.title: Share of consumers who regularly consumed meat substitutes in selected European countries in 2023, by country
charts.short: Consumers who regularly consumed meat substitutes in Europe in 2023, by country
charts.description: In the United Kingdom, about 21 percent of responding consumers stated that they consumed meat substitutes regularly. The average for all countries displayed here was 15 percent of respondents. Populous countries like the UK and Germany are elevating the average with their high number of consumers eating meat substitutes.
charts.note: Europe; July 2022 to June 2023*; 38,993 respondents; 18-64 years
charts.source: Statista; Statista Consumer Insights

charts.title: Revenue in the sweeteners segment of the food market EU-27 from 2019 to 2029 (in billion U.S. dollars)
charts.short: Revenue in the sweeteners segment of the food market EU-27 2019-2029
charts.description: The revenue in the 'Sweeteners' segment of the food market in the European Union was forecast to continuously increase between 2024 and 2029 by in total 1.4 billion U.S. dollars (+21.87 percent). After the tenth consecutive increasing year, the indicator is estimated to reach 7.77 billion U.S. dollars and therefore a new peak in 2029. Notably, the revenue of the 'Sweeteners' segment of the food market was continuously increasing over the past years.
charts.source: Statista

charts.title: Consumption volume in the sweeteners segment of the food market EU-27 from 2019 to 2029 (in billion kilograms)
charts.short: Consumption volume in the sweeteners segment of the food market EU-27 2019-2029
charts.description: The volume in the 'Sweeteners' segment of the food market in the European Union was forecast to continuously increase between 2024 and 2029 by in total 0.3 billion kilograms (+11.9 percent). After the seventh consecutive increasing year, the indicator is estimated to reach 2.79 billion kilograms and therefore a new peak in 2029.
charts.source: Statista

charts.title: Average per capita consumption in the sweeteners segment of the food market EU-27 from 2019 to 2029
charts.short: Average per capita consumption of sweeteners in the EU-27 2019-2029
charts.description: The average volume per capita in the 'Sweeteners' segment of the food market in the European Union was forecast to continuously increase between 2024 and 2029 by in total 0.6 kilograms (+10.64 percent). After the seventh consecutive increasing year, the indicator is estimated to reach 6.28 kilograms and therefore a new peak in 2029.
charts.source: Statista
